text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGE: on-call (OnCallPager) — high error rate hitting /v1/generate. Estimated customer impact 18%. Auto-detection: DB migration 'add_covering_index' started during canary rollout and blocking writes.
OnCallPager: I'm on it, digging into logs.
Alex: seeing 503 spikes from web tier since 09:12 UTC. CPU fine, but request queue length jumped. Backend logs show timeouts waiting on DB.
Samir: Confirmed. Queries piling on primary, many waiting for an exclusive lock. Likely migration DDL holding lock.
Mariya: That migration is a schema change that creates a large index. Migration script didn't use CONCURRENTLY — it was supposed to, but the canary was missing the flag due to a packaging bug.
Elaine: Oh no, the code rolled to 40% of hosts before the feature flag check. Canary should have gated it.
DB-SRE: Running quick checks —
DB-SRE: ```psql -c "select pid, usename, query_start, state, query from pg_stat_activity where query like '%CREATE INDEX%' or query like '%CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY%';"```
DB-SRE: Found index build PID 4129 stuck in 'active' for 7m, lots of waiting backends with 'waiting' state.
Alex: What's the customer-visible failure mode? 503s or errors in our retry layer? Support is getting tickets.
Support: Multiple customers reporting timeouts and slow writes. Small percentage of requests returning 503s, higher for heavier generation loads. No data corruption reports yet.
Mariya: Since index was not concurrent, it acquired an AccessExclusiveLock which blocks reads/writes — that's why writers are queued.
Samir: We need immediate mitigation: options: kill index build and rollback migration, or abort deployment and flip kill-switch feature flag to stop new code paths that rely on the new index.
Elaine: We have a feature flag 'use_new_index' that can be killed. I can flip it across the fleet in ~2 mins. That should stop new requests from hitting the path that enqueues heavy writes, but existing inflight writes may still be blocked.
OnCallPager: Do it. Flip the flag first.
Elaine: Flipped 'use_new_index' to off for production. Rolling out change and verifying. :white_check_mark:
Samir: Good. Also need DB action — killing the index build on primary with pg_cancel_backend might let it fail gracefully. If that fails, pg_terminate_backend. Both have tradeoffs: incomplete index and possible need to re-run migration later.
DB-SRE: Attempting graceful cancel: ```SELECT pg_cancel_backend(4129);```
DB-SRE: Cancel returned true but process still cleaning up; waiting on backend to release lock.
Alex: Observability — request queue length reducing, error rate dropping from 18% -> 6% in last 90s. Support: customers still reporting intermittent 503s.
Support: Noticing some background jobs timed out too, creating retries. Putting a note to suppress noise from pager for now.
DB-SRE: Cancel didn't fully release lock, moving to force terminate: ```SELECT pg_terminate_backend(4129);```
DB-SRE: Terminate succeeded. Index creation rolled back at DB level. Current primary locks cleared.
Samir: Confirming: write throughput back to normal, no long waits in pg_stat_activity.
Mariya: Phew. Since the index build rolled back, we need to: 1) abort current release rollout 2) add CONCURRENTLY to migration + safety checks 3) run migration on replica first, or use background index tooling.
Elaine: Rolling back release now — initiating canary rollback to previous image and pinning flag off.
Elaine: Rollback complete on canary hosts, starting fleet rollback. ETA 8m.
Alex: Runbook reference: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/db-migration-rollback (follow the 'non-concurrent index failure' section).
DB-SRE: Also verifying replicas — replication lag spiked to ~20s during the attempt but is recovering. No failed replication slots.
OnCallPager: Handing off to DB-SRE team for postmortem and cleanup. I'm reassigning incident to Samir (owner) for follow-up and customer comms.
Samir: I'll own follow-up. Immediate action items:
- Create postmortem draft with timeline (owner: Samir)
- Validate no partial indexes present: ```select * from pg_indexes where indexname like '%covering%';``` (owner: DB-SRE)
- Add CI check to ensure migrations that touch large tables require 'use_concurrent_index' flag or fail (owner: Mariya)
- Ensure deploy pipeline enforces feature-flag gating for migrations (owner: Elaine)
- Customer comms: Support to prepare a notice describing service degradation and that no data loss occurred (owner: Support)
Support: Drafting a customer notification now, will coordinate with Samir before send.
Mariya: Adding a temporary safeguard in migration runner to block non-concurrent index creation on prod unless explicit override.
Samir: Estimated customer impact final: 18% requests saw elevated errors for ~11 minutes, after mitigation error rate fell below 1%. No data loss.
IncidentBot: Incident severity: SEV2 (prod degradation). Incident channel will remain open for postmortem notes.
Elaine: Anything else before I close my on-call handoff?
Samir: DB-SRE keep monitoring replicas for next 2 hours, Support watch for any late user reports. I'll start a postmortem doc. Thanks everyone. :pray:
DB-SRE: Monitoring alerts set. Follow-up ticket created: INF-4521.
OnCallPager: Handoff complete.
